rationale: M49-CONV #851 + #852, measured 2026-09-15. Two edge-set defects in groovy's newline-continuation handling, each pinned here beside its own ONE-LINE control, because the control is the contract: the same chain written on one line and written across a continuation must emit the SAME calls multiset, and a member access must stay a read. The pinned grammar shapes a continuation as its own `leading_dot_call` statement node (a documented grammar tradeoff), so (a) `this\n .label` — an extremely common Groovy layout — carried NO argument list and was emitted as `calls -> label`, fabricating a call to a property and losing the read entirely (the same access on one line emits `uses A -> label`), while `helper\n .build(1)` DOES carry `arguments` and is a genuine call; and (b) a continued dotted call folds into `juxt_function_call name: (field_access ...)`, whose whole dotted text became the call target (`helper.build` where the one-line form emits `build`) and whose callee-position field_access additionally leaked a `uses -> build` read that java/kotlin/scala all suppress. The read in the continued form is attributed to the enclosing METHOD rather than the type because the continuation node does not carry its receiver — the GAD1 convention for an unresolvable receiver, which is why `uses A -> label` (line 5) and `uses continuedRead -> label` (line 11) deliberately name different owners for the same member. Every expectation below is the corrected contract read off the source; the forbid entries are the two pre-fix emissions, both measured before the fix on exactly these lines.

expectRelationships.note: CONTROL, unchanged: the same-line `this.label` is a read owned by the type
#851 fixed: the continued `.label` is a READ (pre-fix it was `calls -> label` and no read existed)
#851 boundary: `helper\n .build(1)` DOES carry an argument list, so it stays a call
CONTROL: one line, bare callee leaf
#852 fixed: the continuation's callee is the BARE leaf `build`, the same node the one-line control reaches

forbidRelationships.note: #851 pre-fix: the property read emitted as a CALL, on any line
#852 pre-fix: the whole dotted name stored as the call target, duplicating one method as two graph nodes
#852 pre-fix: the callee leaked as a member READ (a callee is not a read — java/kotlin/scala all suppress it)
